A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, title, optimal-transport formulation and core theorem sequence. All 21 pages of v1 and 28 pages of v2, including their appendices, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports theoretical results and proofs, including Appendix A. Figures 1–2 are conceptual illustrations; no original empirical outcomes are reported.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figure 3 report original solver experiments on Gaussian-mixture transport in dimensions 2 and 4. Appendix C describes their implementation.

M1.justification: The neural parametrization in the learnability construction changes from ReLU ICNNs in v1 Remark 4.4 to CELU ICNNs in v2 Proposition 4.4 and Theorem 4.8. The semi-dual minimax objective and ReLU transport-map network remain unchanged; this is a limited architecture change.

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical dataset coverage. v2 introduces Gaussian-mixture transport experiments in dimensions 2 and 4, mapping a three-Gaussian mixture to an approximate ten-Gaussian mixture with known ground-truth OT maps.

E2.justification: Neither version reports comparisons against competing solvers. v2 uses the Korotin et al. benchmark, but Figure 3 compares experimental errors with fitted lines, not evaluated baseline methods.

E3.justification: v2 introduces an experimental protocol with equal source and target training sizes ranging from 100 to 20,000, 4,096 test samples, and log-log convergence fitting. v1 has no corresponding protocol. Section 5 specifies squared L2 map error, while Appendix C writes the unsquared norm, leaving that implementation detail ambiguous.

E4.justification: Section 5 adds a sample-size sensitivity analysis in two dimensions, providing the first empirical examination of the central convergence-rate prediction. v1 contains no corresponding sensitivity, ablation or robustness analysis.

E5.justification: v2 adds statistical estimation of convergence exponents through log-log linear regression, implemented using numpy.polyfit. Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or error bars; the addition concerns slope estimation rather than uncertainty quantification.

E6.justification: Figure 3 introduces empirical error curves and fitted slopes of -0.728 for dimension 2 and -0.502 for dimension 4. These are newly reported results supporting decreasing error with increasing sample size; v1 has no corresponding measurements to compare directly.

T1.justification: Theorem 4.3 changes compactness to total boundedness. The speculative Remark 4.4 becomes a CELU-based proposition with new proofs, and Theorem 4.6 specifies an approximating class independent of the optimal potential. Appendices A.3.1–A.5 add substantial approximation and Rademacher derivations. The expanded rate proof also invokes zero-mean independent coordinates, which are not stated in Corollary 4.9.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the same central claims: statistical learnability guarantees for quadratic semi-dual minimax OT through error decomposition, Rademacher bounds and arbitrarily small approximation error. The added experiment supports these claims without changing their core scope or reported asymptotic rate.

C2.justification: v1 identifies quadratic cost as its only limitation. v2 additionally discusses strong-convexity requirements, missing lower bounds, and optimization errors that limit practical applicability. Appendix B explains the regularity assumptions, while Appendix C explains why the experimental ICNN architecture differs from the analyzed architecture.

D1.justification: Appendix C newly documents quadratic-skip ICNNs, a transport network with approximately two million parameters, Adam with learning rate 0.001, batch size min(1024, N), 10,000 steps with ten inner map updates per step, and several hours on one A100 GPU. v1 provides no corresponding experimental implementation details.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Benamou and Brenier and to Kingma and Ba. Appendix B further distinguishes practical neural minimax solvers from prior minimax-optimal OT estimators, and Appendix A.4 positions new approximation lemmas relative to Chen et al. The existing related-work framework is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized language and notation clarifications, renames Results to Theoretical Results, and improves proof navigation. It adds Experimental Illustrations and Appendices B–C, while largely retaining the earlier introduction, background, related-work narrative and section order.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two-column to single-column layout, with substantially reflowed equations and removed running headers. Figures 1–2 retain their conceptual content but become integrated with surrounding text, and Figure 3 adds a two-panel convergence plot.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens v1's speculative compactness argument through a supported CELU construction and adds useful empirical context and explicit limitations. However, the expanded rate proof invokes coordinate assumptions absent from its theorem statement, and the small experiment uses a different ICNN architecture with inconsistent squared/unsquared error notation. These issues limit the gain in theoretical and empirical assurance.
